  "text": "The council installed the new streetlamp outside my bedroom on a Tuesday.

By Wednesday, its light had begun arriving late.

A car passed beneath it, but the shadow followed three seconds afterward. Rain glittered in the beam long after the pavement dried.

I phoned the number on the pole.

“Don’t stand underneath it,” the woman said.

Then she asked for my address.

I gave it.

“That one’s been disconnected since March.”

That night, I watched from behind the curtains.

At eleven, a little girl appeared in the light. Red coat. Bare feet. She stood looking up at my window.

I recognised the coat from photographs.

I had worn it when I was six.

The girl lifted one hand.

Against my will, I lifted mine.

She smiled before I did.

I closed the curtains and sat on the bed until morning.

The council sent a man with a ladder. He opened the panel at the lamp’s base, stared inside, then fastened it again.

“Well?” I asked.

He wiped his screwdriver on his trousers.

“Keep your curtains shut.”

That evening, I nailed a blanket across the window.

At eleven, light shone through the nail holes.

Something knocked against the glass.

My phone rang. The council woman.

“Has she reached your age yet?”

From the other side of the blanket came my voice.

“She won’t answer you. She’s frightened.”

The woman inhaled sharply.

“Get out of the room.”

I reached for the door, but my shadow stayed beside the bed.

It raised a finger to its lips.

Outside, the streetlamp went dark.

The room did not."
